edges.description: Heterozygous mice show abnormal striatal and cerebellar synaptic plasticity, and in vivo striatal recordings show aberrant activity and inverted firing-rate modulation during skill learning.
edges.limitations: Mouse cortico-basal ganglia circuitry has no speech output, so the link to the human speech phenotype is by analogy; plasticity has not been measured in affected humans.

edges.description: Homozygous mice show immature cerebellar development and Purkinje cell dendritic abnormalities.
edges.limitations: The cerebellar maldevelopment is a homozygous phenotype; heterozygotes, the genotype matching human patients, have overtly normal brain structure, and the human imaging changes are subtle grey matter differences rather than gross maldevelopment.

edges.description: Ultrasonic vocalizations are used as a readout of vocal motor output; heterozygotes showed modest impairment in one study.
edges.limitations: Mouse pup ultrasonic vocalizations are largely innate rather than learned, so they are a proxy for speech motor output rather than a model of speech motor programming, and a second study found no difference in heterozygous R552H pups.

nodes.description: FOXP2 is expressed during brain development in the cortical plate, basal ganglia, thalamus, inferior olives and cerebellum. Affected KE-family members have bilateral grey matter reductions in the caudate nucleus, cerebellum (notably lobule VIIa Crus I) and inferior frontal gyrus, with increased grey matter in the planum temporale, and underactivate Broca's area, its right homolog and the putamen during language tasks. Caudate and Crus I volumes correlate with oral praxis and nonword repetition performance, linking these motor-related circuits to the speech phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Bilateral brain abnormalities associated with dominantly inherited verbal and orofacial dyspraxia.
evidence.snippet: The most significant findings were reduced grey matter density bilaterally in the caudate nucleus, the cerebellum, and the left and right inferior frontal gyrus in the affected members.

evidence.reference_title: Language fMRI abnormalities associated with FOXP2 gene mutation.
evidence.snippet: the affected members showed significant underactivation relative to the unaffected members in Broca's area and its right homolog, as well as in other cortical language-related regions and in the putamen.

evidence.reference_title: Neocerebellar Crus I Abnormalities Associated with a Speech and Language Disorder Due to a Mutation in FOXP2.
evidence.snippet: We also show that right Crus I volume correlates with left and total caudate nucleus volumes in affected KE members, and that right and total Crus I volumes predict the performance of affected members in non-word repetition and non-verbal orofacial praxis.

nodes.description: Bilaterally reduced caudate nucleus volume and grey matter density in affected KE-family members, most evident in the superior portion and correlated with oral praxis and nonword repetition.

evidence.reference_title: MRI analysis of an inherited speech and language disorder: structural brain abnormalities.
evidence.snippet: The results confirmed that the volume of this nucleus was reduced bilaterally in the affected family members compared with both the unaffected members and the group of age-matched controls.

evidence.reference_title: Neural basis of an inherited speech and language disorder.
evidence.snippet: quantitative analyses of magnetic resonance imaging scans revealed structural abnormalities in several of these same areas, particularly the caudate nucleus, which was found to be abnormally small bilaterally.

nodes.description: Bilateral cerebellar grey matter reduction, localised to neocerebellar lobule VIIa Crus I, which is also hypoactivated during nonword repetition.

evidence.reference_title: Neocerebellar Crus I Abnormalities Associated with a Speech and Language Disorder Due to a Mutation in FOXP2.
evidence.snippet: we provide converging evidence from subsets of affected KE members scanned at three time points for grey matter (GM) volume reduction bilaterally in neocerebellar lobule VIIa Crus I compared with unaffected members and unrelated controls.

evidence.reference_title: Bilateral brain abnormalities associated with dominantly inherited verbal and orofacial dyspraxia.
evidence.snippet: The most significant findings were reduced grey matter density bilaterally in the caudate nucleus, the cerebellum, and the left and right inferior frontal gyrus in the affected members.

nodes.description: Anxiety occurs at increased rates and is a recognised target of mental health surveillance.

nodes.description: Developmental verbal dyspraxia: inconsistent errors on consonants and vowels, lengthened and disrupted coarticulatory transitions, and inappropriate prosody, arising from impaired speech motor planning rather than weakness. It is the most common speech diagnosis in FOXP2-SLD and persists into adulthood, with some speech sounds never acquired.

evidence.reference_title: In-depth characterisation of a cohort of individuals with missense and loss-of-function variants disrupting FOXP2.
evidence.snippet: Speech disorders were prevalent (23/25, 92%) and CAS was most common (22/25, 88%), with similar speech presentations across English and German. Speech was still impaired in adulthood, and some speech sounds (eg, 'th', 'r', 'ch', 'j') were never acquired.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of FOXP2 truncation as a novel cause of developmental speech and language deficits.
evidence.snippet: In multiple members of the well-studied KE family, a heterozygous missense mutation in FOXP2 causes problems in sequencing muscle movements required for articulating speech (developmental verbal dyspraxia), accompanied by wider deficits in linguistic and grammatical processing.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of FOXP2 truncation as a novel cause of developmental speech and language deficits.
evidence.snippet: One such variant is a heterozygous nonsense mutation that yields a dramatically truncated protein product and cosegregates with speech and language difficulties in the proband, his affected sibling, and their mother.

nodes.description: FOXP2 binds promoters in neural chromatin and either represses or activates the genes it occupies; its targets include genes acting in synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, neurotransmission and axon guidance. FOXP2 binds and strongly down-regulates CNTNAP2, a neurexin-family gene expressed in developing cortex. Which targets mediate the speech phenotype is not established, so no edge is drawn from this node to the circuit-level nodes.
nodes.id: Dysregulation of FOXP2 Neural Target Genes

biological_processes: negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

evidence.reference_title: High-throughput analysis of promoter occupancy reveals direct neural targets of FOXP2, a gene mutated in speech and language disorders.
evidence.snippet: Our data indicate that FOXP2 has dual functionality, acting to either repress or activate gene expression at occupied promoters. The identified targets suggest roles in modulating synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, neurotransmission, and axon guidance

evidence.reference_title: A functional genetic link between distinct developmental language disorders.
evidence.snippet: We found that FOXP2 binds to and dramatically down-regulates CNTNAP2, a gene that encodes a neurexin and is expressed in the developing human cortex.

evidence.reference_title: A forkhead-domain gene is mutated in a severe speech and language disorder.
evidence.snippet: In addition, we identify a point mutation in affected members of the KE family that alters an invariant amino-acid residue in the forkhead domain. Our findings suggest that FOXP2 is involved in the developmental process that culminates in speech and language.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of FOXP2 truncation as a novel cause of developmental speech and language deficits.
evidence.snippet: Here, we report investigations of the entire coding region of FOXP2, including alternatively spliced exons, in 49 probands affected with verbal dyspraxia. We detected variants that alter FOXP2 protein sequence in three probands.

evidence.reference_title: Absence of a paternally inherited FOXP2 gene in developmental verbal dyspraxia.
evidence.snippet: We characterize 13 patients with DVD--5 with hemizygous paternal deletions spanning the FOXP2 gene, 1 with a translocation interrupting FOXP2, and the remaining 7 with maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7 (UPD7), who were also given a diagnosis of Silver-Russell Syndrome (SRS).

evidence.reference_title: Speech and language impairment and oromotor dyspraxia due to deletion of 7q31 that involves FOXP2.
evidence.snippet: We propose that this patient, together with others reported in the literature, may define a new contiguous gene deletion syndrome encompassing the 7q31-FOXP2 region.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotype of FOXP2 haploinsufficiency in a mother and son.
evidence.snippet: A 1.57 Mb deletion on chromosome 7q31 was detected by array comparative genomic hybridization (aCGH). In addition to FOXP2, the patients' deletion involves two other genes, MDFIC and PPP1R3A, neither of which has been associated with speech or language disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Functional characterization of rare FOXP2 variants in neurodevelopmental disorder.
evidence.snippet: Of three variants that have been suggested to cause speech/language disorder, but never before been characterized, only one showed functional effects. For the other two, we found no effects on protein function in any assays, suggesting that they are incidental to the phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Speech and Language Disorders Associated With 7q31 Deletions Implicating FOXP2.
evidence.snippet: All verbal individuals had childhood apraxia of speech (5/5, 100%).

evidence.reference_title: Speech and Language Disorders Associated With 7q31 Deletions Implicating FOXP2.
evidence.snippet: The larger the deletion size, the poorer an individual's language skills (p = 0.03, p < 0.05).

nodes.description: Heterozygous loss of FOXP2 transcription-factor function is the shared lesion. The KE-family R553H substitution alters an invariant residue of the forkhead DNA-binding domain and severely impairs nuclear localization and DNA binding; the R328X nonsense allele yields an unstable, mostly cytoplasmic product without transactivation capacity; whole- or partial-gene deletions and translocation breakpoints remove or disrupt one copy.

evidence.reference_title: A forkhead-domain gene is mutated in a severe speech and language disorder.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that the gene FOXP2, which encodes a putative transcription factor containing a polyglutamine tract and a forkhead DNA-binding domain, is directly disrupted by the translocation breakpoint in CS. In addition, we identify a point mutation in affected members of the KE family that alters an invariant amino-acid residue in the forkhead domain.

evidence.reference_title: Functional genetic analysis of mutations implicated in a human speech and language disorder.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the R553H forkhead-box substitution, found in all affected members of a large three-generation family, indicated that it severely affects FOXP2 function, chiefly by disrupting nuclear localization and DNA-binding properties.

evidence.reference_title: Functional genetic analysis of mutations implicated in a human speech and language disorder.
evidence.snippet: The R328X truncation mutation, segregating with speech/language disorder in a second family, yields an unstable, predominantly cytoplasmic product that lacks transactivation capacity.

evidence.reference_title: FOXP2-Related Speech and Language Disorder.
evidence.snippet: FOXP2-related speech and language disorder (FOXP2-SLD) is caused by heterozygous FOXP2 pathogenic variants (including whole- or partial-gene deletions).

nodes.description: An independently generated R552H knock-in line. Homozygotes show immature cerebellar development with poorly arborised Purkinje cells, severe ultrasonic vocalization and motor impairment, and early death; heterozygotes show modest ultrasonic vocalization impairments with altered call qualities. A separate study of R552H and null (S321X) pups found that heterozygotes' innate vocalizations did not differ from wild type, so the vocal phenotype in heterozygotes is not consistent across studies.

evidence.reference_title: Ultrasonic vocalization impairment of Foxp2 (R552H) knockin mice related to speech-language disorder and abnormality of Purkinje cells.
evidence.snippet: we generated a knockin (KI) mouse for Foxp2 (R552H) ... corresponding to the human FOXP2 (R553H) mutation, by homologous recombination.

nodes.description: ENU-derived mice carrying the arginine-to-histidine substitution equivalent to the KE-family R553H. Heterozygotes have overtly normal brain structure and baseline motor ability but slower motor-skill learning and abnormal striatal and cerebellar synaptic plasticity; homozygotes have reduced cerebellar growth and die postnatally.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we generated mice carrying an identical point mutation to that of the KE family, yielding the equivalent arginine-to-histidine substitution in the Foxp2 DNA-binding domain.

nodes.description: A deficit in learning and producing sequences of movement, or in procedural learning, has been proposed as the common basis of the verbal and nonverbal deficits of affected KE-family members. Foxp2 R552H heterozygous mice have normal baseline motor ability but learn species-typical motor skills more slowly.

evidence.snippet: Affected individuals are characterized by deficits in the learning and production of complex orofacial motor sequences underlying fluent speech and display impaired linguistic processing for both spoken and written language.

The human counterpart has not been measured directly.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, there were dramatic alterations in striatal plasticity during the acquisition of a motor skill, with most neurons in mutants showing negative modulation of firing rate, starkly contrasting with the predominantly positive modulation seen in control animals.

nodes.description: One route to FOXP2 deficiency is absence of the paternal copy, through a paternally derived 7q31 deletion or translocation, or through maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 7 (which also causes Silver-Russell syndrome). Losing the paternal allele lowers FOXP2 dosage; whether the maternal allele is also relatively underexpressed (imprinting) is disputed, since one study found maternal underexpression and a later one found FOXP2 is not imprinted (PMID:23033221, no abstract).
